common_acceptance: Authoritative campaign/actor/source/rules-version/class-level eligibility; isolated high-level test entitlements grant no production access. Prepare previews costs/choices/targets/timing without dice or writes; explicit confirm revalidates current revision and commits choices, injectable dice, resource/action costs, effects, derived sheet and public history atomically. Store durable action receipt: same-ID retry/reload/reconnect returns exact committed result with no reroll/recharge/regrant; conflicting payload or concurrent stale confirmation rejected; two concurrent confirmations spend/apply once. Inject history/effect/choice failure and prove full PostgreSQL rollback. Protect private NPC HP, hidden actors, tactics and private choices in discovery/preview/history/error/reconnect. Shared web/TUI availability, disabled reason, accessible confirmation/cancel and reconnect fixtures required; desktop/phone confirmation journeys for changed web UI. Unknown prerequisites fail closed. Run GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p2 -short -race ./... and go vet -p2 ./...; isolated PostgreSQL integration rollback/replay/reload/concurrency tests; frontend build, changed-file lint and behavior fixtures when UI changes. Preserve legacy reads/unrelated JSON; retain CC-BY-4.0 attribution and adaptations. No production deployment, inference or broad coverage promotion.

<!-- edda-323:qualification-gate -->
Native parent #323; decision #323; roadmap #47; directly blocks #337. Task Size M.

One qualification PR after accepted323 decision and every exact mandatory terminal below. Source pinned SRD5.2.1 PDF19-25/36-40/87-88/97/104-106/107-175/174-191; SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution/adaptation docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md.

Acceptance: reconcile every83 Cleric/Life source record,193 unique keys, all20rows/9slot columns, entry, nested options, improvements and all20 applications against exact committed positive/negative source-linked fixtures. Fixed Human Acolyte Cleric1 and isolated caster effects are narrow compatibility evidence only. Missing effects block qualification, never silently excluded. No runtime mechanics or grants in qualification PR.

Authoritative campaign/actor/source/rules-version/class-level eligibility; isolated high-level test entitlements grant no production access. Prepare previews costs/choices/targets/timing without dice or writes; explicit confirm revalidates current revision and commits choices, injectable dice, resource/action costs, effects, derived sheet and public history atomically. Store durable action receipt: same-ID retry/reload/reconnect returns exact committed result with no reroll/recharge/regrant; conflicting payload or concurrent stale confirmation rejected; two concurrent confirmations spend/apply once. Inject history/effect/choice failure and prove full PostgreSQL rollback. Protect private NPC HP, hidden actors, tactics and private choices in discovery/preview/history/error/reconnect. Shared web/TUI availability, disabled reason, accessible confirmation/cancel and reconnect fixtures required; desktop/phone confirmation journeys for changed web UI. Unknown prerequisites fail closed. Run GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p2 -short -race ./... and go vet -p2 ./...; isolated PostgreSQL integration rollback/replay/reload/concurrency tests; frontend build, changed-file lint and behavior fixtures when UI changes. Preserve legacy reads/unrelated JSON; retain CC-BY-4.0 attribution and adaptations. No production deployment, inference or broad coverage promotion.

#382 retains native parent323, after351 and direct279/280/337 edges; this gate consumes382 without replacing it. #498/#501 and historical334 edges remain unchanged. Spell/list membership and execution are distinct: #503 membership, #279 actual spell/effect qualification, #280 item qualification. World effects consume exact #181/#185 contracts and #183 qualification. Chosen feats require384-401 source/terminal evidence.

Every listed prerequisite is a direct native blocker, at most100. Verify strict terminal -> this gate ->337 paths, parent containment and prerequisite cycles separately. Decision closure is not class qualification. Leave323 open for its decision PR and this gate open for independent acceptance.

47.title: [Roadmap] Story-led Edda gameplay with SRD 5.2.1
47.body:
<!-- roadmap-slicer:edda-story-led-srd-521:roadmap -->

<!-- edda-remaining-plan:start -->
## Remaining execution plan — November 16 UTC / November 15 Chicago

[Complete roadmap and development plan](https://github.com/subculture-collective/edda/blob/4ae44d2f4d0b5216c474211d9010d17920b179c6/docs/remaining-development-plan.md) · [All-issue dependency snapshot](https://github.com/subculture-collective/edda/blob/4ae44d2f4d0b5216c474211d9010d17920b179c6/docs/remaining-issues.json) · Documentation PR #345.

The refreshed snapshot has **200 open issues: 11 tracking issues and 189 work issues**. Every remaining issue is listed once in the plan, with its native parent, open blockers, dependency wave and verification requirements. This section is the current execution guidance; the original waves below retain delivery history.

1. **Qualify the current playable slice (3 issues): #46 → #78 → #89.** Record the visible phone-keyboard and human/accessibility evidence, reuse the qualification work in #343, and retain the declared partial-coverage boundary. #342 is closed through #344; its exact Athletics request prepares a preview and does not enable general SRD free text.
2. **Safe contracts and useful gameplay (19 issues):** start #143, #194, #195 and #284 alongside the qualification lane. Then prefer the bounded #338/#339 Fighter actions, #148 Bandit, #263 → #266 ally healing, and #145 → #264 light. The plan enumerates all 15 runtime slices and their exact prerequisites.
3. **Source catalogues (132 data PRs):** #151–#178/#184 monsters, #196–#224 spells, #225–#262 items/equipment and #285–#320 characters. Each follows its own contract; data alone cannot enable playable support.
4. **Remaining mechanics (31 investigations plus future implementation PRs):** begin ready shared-effect decisions #271/#273 early; run class and residual-key decisions after their actual source prerequisites. Publish bounded implementation children and make every terminal implementation block the corresponding full gate before closing a decision.
5. **Full coverage (4 gates): #183 world, #279 spells, #280 items and #337 characters.** Keep #54 open until every required domain and its explicit exit criteria qualify. Current-slice qualification is independent of these full-coverage gates.

These delivery groups overlap. Native blocked-by links define **five current dependency waves with 20 / 140 / 25 / 3 / 1 work issues**. The ready frontier is #46, #143–#147, #194/#195, #268–#276, #284 and #338/#339. This is eligibility, not a request to start all items concurrently or apply automation labels.

The longest currently known remaining chain is **#194 → a spell batch such as #196 → #277 → #279 → #280**. The 31 investigations will add implementation prerequisites, so the current graph gives a lower bound and cannot support a credible Full Rules completion date.

#48/#50/#51 have no open native work children at capture; review their exit evidence during #89 before closing those trackers. Closed issue checkboxes below have been reconciled with GitHub state. Phone/human gates remain open.
<!-- edda-remaining-plan:end -->

Deliver readable story-led play, an interactive rules-backed character sheet, grounded action assistance and faithful chapters across desktop and phone, while keeping the main gameplay screen within one viewport like the current app.

## How to use this roadmap

This roadmap and its epics are tracking issues, not implementation PRs. Each work issue is **one reviewable PR**, and native GitHub dependencies set the order: an issue is ready when every issue it depends on is closed. Close a work issue from its merged PR with `Closes #<n>`. Tracking issues depend on their children, so they close last.

Plan: [Detailed product and implementation plan](https://github.com/subculture-collective/edda/blob/c2beafa55ff18b8d880096dcba56914a6870ed29/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-14-story-led-rules-gameplay.md), source commit `c2beafa`. The plan defines the complete target; work below is split into reviewable PRs and bounded investigations.

## Decisions

- SRD 5.2.1 is the pinned rules reference; use one authoritative server rules/action path.
- Story-led play; interactive sheet with targets/options/costs; rolls happen on confirmation with inspectable results.
- Narrative combat with initiative, explicit range/conditions and target selection; no required grid UI.
- Main gameplay fits one viewport on desktop and phone, with internal transcript/detail scrolling and anchored reachable action controls.
- Preserve the current Art Deco design language and the overall choice-based campaign creation process.
- Ghost text accepts with Tab or touch into an editable draft; accepting a suggestion never submits it.
- Faithful chapters follow played outcomes without invented events or hidden lore.

## Epics

- [ ] #48 Make campaign actions private, durable and recoverable: 12 PR(s). Reuse the review findings to protect campaign ownership, action order, persistence and client recovery.
- [ ] #49 Keep story-led gameplay usable within one screen: 10 PR(s). Refresh the Art Deco reading surface, bounded panels, anchored controls and desktop/phone navigation.
- [ ] #50 Play supported SRD actions from the interactive sheet: 13 PR(s). Deliver small vertical slices for skills, attacks, items, narrative combat and casting.
- [ ] #51 Create and advance valid rules-versioned characters: 8 PR(s). Retain the chosen setup process while validating supported builds and preserving legacy campaigns.
- [x] #52 Offer useful player-known action suggestions and reminders: 6 PR(s). Connect intentional provider/memory routing to grounded suggestions, Tab/touch acceptance and return reminders.
- [x] #53 Read and export faithful campaign chapters: 4 PR(s). Turn committed player-visible play into durable chapters with a reader, source links and fidelity checks.
- [ ] #54 Complete and qualify the declared SRD 5.2.1 coverage: 191 tracked work issues, including expansion follow-ups. Track the full rules/content target through source-linked batch decisions, implementation follow-ups and qualification.

## Original execution waves (history)

Work top to bottom. Issues in the same wave do not depend on each other and can run in parallel.

### Wave 1: can start now

- [x] #28 Enforce campaign ownership across all campaign actions and resources (L, needs a human)
- [x] #55 Select screen-fitting desktop and phone gameplay concepts (M, spike, needs a human)
- [ ] #46 Assess narrow-screen campaign play before redesigning the HUD (M, spike, needs a human)
- [x] #56 Pin SRD 5.2.1 and establish explicit rules coverage (M)
- [x] #31 Repair the database integration suite's fact-visibility assertion (S)
- [x] #45 Add behavior regression coverage before the frontend overhaul (M)
- [x] #40 Honor configured model routes for world creation and summaries (M)
- [x] #44 Complete keyboard and screen-reader behavior for campaign tabs (M)
- [x] #39 Allow semantic campaign memory with non-Ollama game-master providers (M)

### Wave 2

- [x] #57 Keep legacy characters separate from SRD-versioned campaigns (M; after #56)
- [x] #29 Prevent overlapping campaign turns from saving duplicate turn numbers (M; after #31)
- [x] #42 Investigate stale narrative and live events when switching campaigns (M, spike; after #45)
- [x] #37 Investigate turn-stream cleanup when the live client disconnects (M, spike; after #45)
- [x] #43 Measure and bound live-event retention during long play sessions (M, spike; after #45)
- [x] #60 Keep the gameplay frame within the desktop and phone viewport (M; after #55, #45)
- [x] #33 Recover cleanly from interrupted or failed campaign creation (L; after #31)
- [x] #34 Report failures when campaign rules, clock or starting abilities cannot be initialized (M; after #31)
- [x] #35 Do not report a campaign rules mode that failed to save (S; after #31)
- [x] #38 Enable the API server's automatic campaign summaries (M; after #40)
- [x] #36 Make Start Over reset campaign history, saves and time atomically (M; after #31)
- [x] #32 Gate pull requests on database-backed integration tests (M; after #31)

### Wave 3

- [x] #109 Release consumed live events using a bounded sequence/acknowledgment contract (M; after #43)

- [x] #58 Expose a typed rules-derived character sheet projection (L; after #57)
- [x] #30 Keep campaign state consistent when a turn fails after applying changes (L; after #28, #29)
- [x] #62 Keep choices and action drafts usable in the screen-fitting composer (M; after #60)
- [x] #71 Expose Character, World and Journal context without losing the story (M; after #60, #44)
- [x] #90 Improve transcript reading inside the fixed gameplay frame (M; after #60)

### Wave 4

- [x] #59 Recover narration after a committed action without rerolling (L; after #30)
- [x] #61 Resolve SRD checks and saving throws with inspectable dice receipts (M; after #58)
- [ ] #78 Assert gameplay viewport fit, scroll ownership and control reachability (M, needs a human; after #62, #71, #46)

### Wave 5

- [x] #63 Preview a character action without consuming resources (M; after #61, #28)
- [x] #70 Generate a durable faithful chapter from committed campaign history (L; after #59, #40)
- [x] #41 Stream narrative text incrementally during turn generation (M; after #59, #37)

### Wave 6

- [x] #105 Decide turn ownership and detect silent-provider disconnects (M; after #59)

- [x] #64 Confirm prepared actions once and reconcile the committed result (L; after #63, #30, #62)
- [x] #75 Suggest relevant actions from player-known scene and character state (M; after #63, #42)
- [x] #76 Read campaign chapters with navigation and retained position (M; after #70, #71)

### Wave 7

- [x] #65 Play a martial attack through the interactive character sheet (L; after #64)
- [x] #79 Use a consumable from the sheet with one durable cost (M; after #64)
- [x] #84 Accept faint action completions with Tab or touch without submitting (M; after #75, #62)
- [x] #85 Help returning players recall their current situation without spoilers (M; after #75, #38)
- [x] #86 Export faithful chapters with source and rules provenance (M; after #76)
- [x] #87 Qualify chapter fidelity with curated plot and hidden-lore fixtures (M, needs a human; after #76)

### Wave 8

- [x] #66 Track initiative and action economy in narrative combat (L; after #65)
- [x] #69 Create a valid SRD martial character through the existing choice flow (L; after #65, #33, #34, #35)

### Wave 9

- [x] #67 Validate narrative combat targets, ranges and scene facts (L; after #66)
- [x] #81 Offer explicit reaction choices at the correct combat trigger (M; after #66)

### Wave 10

- [x] #68 Cast a supported spell with explicit targets and slot costs (L; after #67)
- [x] #82 Split remaining SRD monster and exploration rules into PR-sized batches (M, spike; after #67, #81)

### Wave 11

- [x] #72 Create a valid SRD caster with prepared spells and resources (M; after #69, #68)
- [x] #77 Track concentration, durations and recovery for the casting slice (L; after #68)

### Wave 12

- [x] #73 Advance a supported character using SRD progression choices (M; after #72)
- [x] #80 Split remaining SRD spells, items and effects into PR-sized batches (M, spike; after #77, #79)
- [x] #83 Validate interview-generated characters against the same rules catalogue (M; after #72)

### Wave 13

- [x] #74 Split remaining SRD character and advancement coverage into PR-sized batches (M, spike; after #73)
- [x] #88 Expose actual rules coverage and prevent premature Full Rules claims (M; after #73)

### Wave 14

- [ ] #89 Qualify the declared gameplay slice across desktop, phone and reconnects (L, needs a human; after #88, #78, #84, #87, #83, #77, #79, #81, #86, #85, #36)

## Original declared-slice critical path (history)

#56 → #57 → #58 → #61 → #63 → #64 → #65 → #66 → #67 → #68 → #72 → #73 → #88 → #342 → #89

15 issues, 38 size points on the declared-slice path (S=1, M=2, L=3). Start these first; splitting work on this chain shortens the roadmap.

## Shared delivery rules

- Every work issue is one reviewable PR; spikes finish with a recorded decision and bounded follow-up issues.
- Reuse review issues #28-#46; evidence and original acceptance criteria are retained. No automation/agent queue labels are applied.
- Preserve legacy modes, data, public routes and the shared web/TUI boundary; new rules support is versioned and explicitly partial until qualified.
- Viewport contract: no document overflow at the specified default desktop/tablet/phone sizes; long content scrolls internally; keyboard-open and accessibility reflow require separate checks.
- Full coverage remains an epic exit criterion. Character/spell/world expansion spikes publish exact follow-up PRs into this roadmap and extend native dependencies; initial batches are not the whole SRD.
- No implementation, deployment, destructive conversion or production data mutation is authorized by publication.
- Size L warnings are retained only for a named integration boundary or fixture. They are review-size estimates, not delivery dates; split and update the graph if evidence exceeds that boundary.
- The final campaign qualification joins independent completed capabilities, so its real prerequisite fan-in exceeds five. Transitive prerequisite edges are removed; no artificial serial chain was introduced to hide this warning.

## Out of scope

- A tactical grid editor, new brand, cooperative multiplayer, non-SRD commercial catalogue, marketplace, native app and unrelated infrastructure changes.

## Wave 2 investigation decisions

#42 reproduced cross-campaign contamination and fixed hook isolation in PR #103. #37 contained blocked stream publication in PR #107; silent-provider disconnect detection and ownership remain #105. #43 measured unbounded transport retention in PR #110; its bounded consumption implementation is #109. These follow-ups are children of #48 and prerequisites of final qualification #89. Completing the spikes does not claim those follow-up capabilities are implemented.

<!-- edda-wave10-world-expansion:start -->
## World expansion follow-ups from Wave 10 (#82)

Decision: [source inventory and batch plan](https://github.com/subculture-collective/edda/blob/20a5b78/docs/investigations/issue-82-world-expansion.md), PR #186. The hash-verified inventory contains 331 indexed monster/animal entries plus four spell-created creature blocks, all currently unsupported.

43 bounded follow-ups belong to epic #54: 29 data batches (at most 12 records each), nine contract/runtime slices, four bounded spikes and full-world qualification #183. ## Wave 14 independent qualification

[Candidate evidence](https://github.com/subculture-collective/edda/blob/d103c0b/docs/playtest/issue-89/README.md) is in draft PR #343. Local evidence passes: 64 frontend unit tests, 93 Chromium browser cases with one worker and unchanged timeouts/assertions, build, focused changed-file lint, full Go short race/vet, disposable PostgreSQL handler/state suites and TUI fixtures. Whole-tree frontend lint retains 22 baseline errors. These are separate component/contract fixtures, not a single continuous real-browser/real-database campaign or a production deployment.

The candidate fixes explicit same-action recovery after a server error, with campaign ID isolation and optimistic-entry/history reconciliation. It intentionally leaves #89 open: the fresh Android attempt again hit DEVICE_IN_USE owned by another session, and a final human player-experience review is not recorded. #46/#78 remain open.

Real PostgreSQL evidence also exposes the SRD free-text gap: typed actions succeed, but ordinary text reaches the intentional legacy guard. #342 is a bounded implementation under #50, with prerequisites #64/#88, Size L, and a native blocker of #89. It prepares only `Make an Athletics check` through the authoritative preview/explicit-confirm path; arbitrary text and legacy mutations stay unavailable. Independent implementation is proceeding in a separate PR; no unsupported pass is claimed here.

263.title: Cast level-one Cure Wounds on one willing adjacent ally
263.body:
<!-- roadmap-slicer:edda-story-led-srd-521:issue:spell-items-cure-ally -->

Epic: #191 · Parent coverage: #54 · Roadmap: #47 · Decision: #80

Source: [pinned SRD 5.2.1, PDF pp. 14–17, 105–106, 121](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/srd/5.2/SRD_CC_v5.2.1.pdf). Pin, license and attribution: `docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md`. Decision/inventory: `docs/investigations/issue-80-spell-item-expansion.md` and `issue-80-spell-item-inventory.json`.

**Delivery: one reviewable PR (M).**

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Prepare one player-known, willing, conscious allied creature within touch reach with explicit eligibility/components; reject hidden, distant or unresolved targets.
- [ ] Save one level-one slot, capped 2d8 plus Wisdom healing, target and dice receipt atomically. Retry/reload cannot heal/spend twice; injected history failure rolls back all effects.
- [ ] Desktop/phone fixtures require target and slot confirmation. Preserve self-casting and legacy behavior; other slots and target/condition exceptions remain unavailable.

## Blocked by

- #67
- #194

## Verification

- `go test -short -race ./...` and `go vet ./...`.
- For mutations: isolated PostgreSQL handler/state integration tests with injectable dice, rollback, receipt replay and reload.
- For UI: frontend build, changed-file lint, behavior fixtures and desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect journeys.
- Data-only work: offline source/schema/name/variant fixtures, no inference or production data.
- Spikes: publish/read back child issues, native hierarchy and exact blocking edges to the qualification gates before closing.

## Boundaries and exclusions

Start in `internal/rules/srd521`, `internal/game`, `internal/engine`, `internal/combat` and relevant handler/character UI fixtures. Preserve legacy reads and the shared web/TUI engine. Unknown mechanics remain unavailable. No adjacent batches, production mutation, hidden-lore disclosure or unsupported Full Rules claims. Source-derived data retains CC-BY-4.0 attribution and adaptation notices. Close work from its merged PR.

351.title: Track two Shield of Faith casters with independent recipient effects
351.body:
<!-- edda-271:effect-identity -->

Parent: #193 · Decision: #271 · Roadmap: #47. One reviewable PR; L; afk. Implementation fixture; not full spell/family support.

Source: [pinned SRD 5.2.1](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/srd/5.2/SRD_CC_v5.2.1.pdf), PDF pages 105, 106, 162, 179. SHA-256 `8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87`. Pin, attribution and adaptation: `docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md`.

## Exact fixture

Two explicitly prepared level-one Clerics cast Shield of Faith at separate times on one known creature within 60 feet, then one caster ends concentration.

## Targets

One known same-campaign creature per cast; retain the existing conscious-self path. Require authoritative range and clear path; reject unknown range, total cover, foreign or hidden recipients.

## Costs

Each cast: one level-one slot, Bonus Action, V/S and noncostly material/focus availability; one-slot-per-turn limit. Voluntary ending: no action or slot refund.

## Timing and mechanic boundary

Absolute start/expiry seconds, maximum 600 seconds. Replace only the casting caster’s previous concentration. Equal-potency overlapping +2 AC applies once, latest casting active; ending it reveals an older still-live effect without restarting its clock.

Proposed mechanic keys (planning identifiers, not registered support): `effect.instance.caster-recipient`, `effect.same-spell.latest-equal`, `effect.duration.absolute`, `concentration.owner`. Reconcile with #194/#277/#278; keep unknown keys unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Persist cast identity separately from recipient links; remove all links only for the ended cast. Different casters never overwrite each other. Preserve old self-only saves and unrelated stats.
- [ ] Prove same caster replacement, different caster overlap, equal potency tie, exact expiry, older effect resumption, independent targets and no doubled AC. Different spell AC terms retain their own rules.
- [ ] Durable mutation fixtures: lock/revalidate all involved actors and effect revisions; save costs, dice, effect/link state, clock/turn and history in one transaction. Inject history-write failure and prove complete rollback; retry same action ID returns the committed receipt with no extra roll, charge or effect. Reload/reconnect resumes exact identities and pending timing.
- [ ] Disclosure negatives: preview never rolls/writes; reject foreign campaign/actor IDs, hidden recipients and forged costs/timing; public receipts omit private NPC HP, unobserved spells and tactics. Unknown facts fail closed with an explicit reason. Preserve unrelated JSON and legacy reads.
- [ ] For higher-level isolated fixtures, demonstrate authoritative test entitlement explicitly; do not treat imported spell data or closing a class investigation as player eligibility. Publish any missing production-eligibility implementation prerequisite before enabling discovery.

## Hard prerequisites

- #194
- #218

Only these are hard prerequisites: source record/contract owners and the exact shared fixture named above. Class production eligibility stays unavailable where explicitly excluded. Every terminal implementation directly blocks both #279 and #280. A spike must add all of its resulting terminal implementation blockers to both gates before closure; decision closure supplies no playable evidence.

## Verification

`go test -short -race ./...` and `go vet ./...`. Runtime PRs must additionally run isolated PostgreSQL handler tests with `-tags=integration`, injectable dice, rollback, receipt replay and reload (short tests do not include them). Changed UI requires build/lint and desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect journeys. Spike PRs validate source/manifest and read back every published body, parent and dependency, checking acyclicity.

## Boundaries and exclusions

Start in `internal/rules/srd521`, `internal/game`, `internal/engine`, `internal/combat` and relevant handler fixtures. Keep the shared web/TUI action path; no production migration execution or deployment. No arbitrary potency comparator, Bless, multiple targets per cast, item activation, new character creation, or blanket spell support. No Full Rules claim. Retain CC-BY-4.0 attribution and mark adaptations. Close from the merged PR.

352.title: Apply one level-one Bless cast to up to three explicit recipients
352.body:
<!-- edda-271:bless-recipients -->

Parent: #193 · Decision: #271 · Roadmap: #47. One reviewable PR; L; afk. Implementation fixture; not full spell/family support.

Source: [pinned SRD 5.2.1](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/srd/5.2/SRD_CC_v5.2.1.pdf), PDF pages 105, 106, 113, 179. SHA-256 `8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87`. Pin, attribution and adaptation: `docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md`.

## Exact fixture

One prepared level-one Cleric casts Bless on self and two known creatures; one recipient makes a supported attack and another makes a supported saving throw.

## Targets

One to three distinct known same-campaign creatures within 30 feet and a clear path. Validate every target before any write. No hidden actor enumeration.

## Costs

One level-one slot and Magic action, V/S and an owned Holy Symbol worth at least 5 GP (not consumed). Verify the explicit priced material; an arbitrary focus cannot substitute for it. A d4 per affected attack roll or saving throw, no cost per recipient.

## Timing and mechanic boundary

Concentration up to 60 seconds; one cast identity owns all recipient links. Overlapping equal Bless casts give one d4, latest live effect; caster ending removes only that cast.

Proposed mechanic keys (planning identifiers, not registered support): `effect.recipients.explicit-set`, `roll.bless.d4`, `effect.same-spell.latest-equal`. Reconcile with #194/#277/#278; keep unknown keys unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Apply recorded d4 to supported attacks and saves only, including concentration Constitution saves; never ability checks, damage rolls or repeated preview.
